mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q-o-q for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises >0.3pp for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates contracting manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >0.5% m-o-m for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a fall in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.4% in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises >0.25% m-o-m AND CPIAUCSL falls >0.4% m-o-m
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.4%) in at least 50% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls >1% m-o-m AND HOUST falls >1% m-o-m in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of co-triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for at least six consecutive months indicates a deep labor market slack, which erodes consumer purchasing power and corporate pricing power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 3% signals robust aggregate demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days in non-recessionary regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered expansions.
